newsitem.title: VATICAN: Pope appoints coadjutor for Hong Kong bishop.
newsitem.headline: Pope appoints coadjutor for Hong Kong bishop.

text.p: Pope John Paul on Sunday named a Chinese-born coadjutor, effectively a successor in waiting, to the bishop of Hong Kong in the British-ruled colony which reverts to China next year.
A Vatican statement said the Pontiff had appointed 64-year-old Shanghai-born Salesian Joseph Zeng as coadjutor to the bishop, 71-year-old Cardinal John Baptist Wu Cheng-chung.
The Vatican said the Pope had also named Monsignor John Tong, born in the colony in 1939, as an auxiliary to Wu.
The nominations may prove controversial since Catholics in communist China are allowed to worship openly only if they belong to the state-sponsored Catholic Patriotic Association (CPA).
The CPA appoints its own bishops and does not recognise the Pope as universal Catholic leader.
Vatican relations with Beijing have alternately cooled and warmed over the decades since the late 1950s, when links were severed over the Vatican's recognition of Taiwan.
China has said it will not normalise relations until the Vatican severs ties with Taiwan, which Beijing has regarded as a rebel province since the end of the Chinese civil war in 1949.
